{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back.   backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back.   (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on

  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block

  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. {"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

{"content":"# gh-1516 — FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: An interactive TUI session with `approvalMode: autopilot` runs the full gh-1412 FinalizeGate ritual (verification shell calls + checklist) on every final answer, including trivial Q&A, and an unfenced `task-ledger` dump stays visible in the transcript.

**Root cause**: The FinalizeGate is keyed on the wrong axis. Both attachment points use the approval MODE (a permission policy) as a proxy for ATTENDANCE (whether a human is watching):

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:649` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.approvalMode == ApprovalMode.unattended;`
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:53-56` — `_withFinalizeGate` appends `finalizeGateContractPrompt` to the system prompt under the same condition.

`ApprovalMode.unattended` ("autopilot") is also a legitimate interactive-TUI choice (skip the critical bash interceptor while a human watches every turn). The actual attendance signal already exists: `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — set by the executable's dispatch for `fa -p` / bench runs (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:1207`), false for the interactive REPL/TUI.

**Impact**:
- Interactive TUI in autopilot: `finalizeGateContractPrompt` rides the system prompt → the model performs the checklist + real-command verification ritual on EVERY final answer, even pure Q&A with zero produced state (the reported 4+ pointless shell calls around a plain-text answer).
- `parseTaskLedger` (`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`) only recognizes the FENCED ```task-ledger block; the near-miss shape models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) is neither parsed into a hidden record nor stripped → ledger garbage stays visible in the transcript.
- The contract prompt has no trivial-turn exception, so even a correct headless run gets the ritual on Q&A turns.

**Fix approach**:
1. **Attendance, not permission**: key both the `finalizeGate` flag and `_withFinalizeGate` on `config.headlessRun`. Interactive (any approval mode) = gate off; headless `-p`/bench = gate on (any approval mode).
2. **Skip trivial turns**: prompt clause (pure Q&A = no checklist/ledger) + loop-level: no tool calls in the run ⇒ no `TaskLedgerEvent` (nothing to verify). The ledger is still stripped from the final message whenever present, so the transcript never shows it.
3. **Tolerant parse + strip**: `parseTaskLedger` also accepts the unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet shape (only when it yields requirement-bearing entries); new `stripTaskLedger` removes the ledger (fenced or unfenced) from the answer text; the loop rewrites the final assistant message with the stripped text before `AgentEndEvent` so the persisted/rendered transcript is clean.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — fresh bug (regression introduced by gh-1412, merged 2026-10-08 in #1418).

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. 'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

messages.preview: 'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — …

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

messages.preview: 'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — …

blocks.text:
'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.'

'You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a127a5-3ed1-7309-b8de-ba21ce7b47b6/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender\'s address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.\n'
            'When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project\'s file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).\n'
            '\n'
            'Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host\'s config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.\n'
            '\n'
            '## The owner talks to you only\n'
            '\n'
            'The owner\'s messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner\'s address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child\'s result lands, report it back. arguments.content:
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

{"content":"## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

{"content":"## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.
